chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with a woman and kissed her, provided that he had not ejaculated into her, and then he married her daughter. He said: If he had not ejaculated into the mother, there is no harm (in marrying the daughter); but if he had ejaculated into her, he should not marry her daughter.

key_terms.أَفْضَى: To ejaculate (specifically in the context of consummation)
key_terms.الْأُمّ: The mother (in this context, the woman he had relations with)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry a woman's daughter if the father had previously had intercourse with her?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of marrying the daughter hinges on the specific act of ejaculation (istifda') with the mother, distinguishing this from mere intercourse or kissing. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the depth of sexual connection in establishing familial barriers, contrasting with other schools that may consider any penetration sufficient. The hadith underscores the precision required in deriving legal consequences from specific physical acts within the context of marriage eligibility.
